meta.title: Riemann 1 V1
meta.prompt: I want to resod my lawn this summer. Each roll of sod is 1 foot wide. The graph below is a map of my lawn. I want to ensure that each strip of sod is long enough to extend past the edge of the lawn, so that no part of the lawn is left uncovered. Thinking of the area of the lawn in terms a Riemann sum, for each interval below, decide whether we should use the left endpoint, right endpoint, or midpoint to determine the length of each strip of sod. Graph of a polynomial function in the first quadrant creating an area under a curve. \begin{tikzpicture} \pgfplotsset{grid style={dashed,darkgray}} \begin{axis}[ axis on top, xtick={1,3,5,7,9,11}, ytick={4,8,12,16}, ymin=-0.5,ymax=16, xmin=-.5,xmax=12.5, grid=both ] \addplot [firstcurvestyle,areastyle,domain=1:11] {-.015*(x-4)*(x-2)*(x-6)*(x-12)+10} \closedcycle; \addplot [firstcurvestyle,domain=1:11,samples=100] {-.015*(x-4)*(x-2)*(x-6)*(x-12)+10}; \draw [firstcolor,thick] (axis cs:1,0) -- (axis cs:1,7.5) (axis cs:11,0) -- (axis cs:11,14.725); \end{axis} \end{tikzpicture}
